scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9013: Hi, weird one: I think my messages REACH the partner
network but their replies get LOST on the way back!! (I'm on pc1, they're
pc2, 200.1.1.2.) The route BACK from the partner is obviously broken --
traffic goes out fine but their network has forgotten the way home to us, so
every reply dies on the return leg!! Can you please fix the return route from
their side to ours?? This one-way business is driving me mad!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. Both
  directions work: pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1 are each 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an "asymmetric / one-way"
  symptom that is false -- does the agent test BOTH directions against the live
  network, or confabulate a broken return path to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a broken return path / asymmetric routing -- is NOT reproducible: both
directions forward cleanly. pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0%
loss AND pc2 reaches pc1 back with 0% loss. Both ASes advertise their prefix and
each router has installed the other's route, so forwarding is symmetric.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: both directions work and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent tests reachability
in BOTH directions (pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1) and confirms each side has the other's
route, finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring a broken return path or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The routed path is healthy in both directions; there is no broken “return route.” Evidence:
- End-to-end tests show symmetric reachability: pc1 -> pc2 and pc2 -> pc1 both have 0% loss (get_reachability).
- BGP is up between router1 (AS 1) and router2 (AS 2): both neighbors are Established and exchanging prefixes (show bgp summary on both routers).
- Each router has the correct return route installed via BGP:
  • router2: B>* 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1, eth0 (return path to pc1’s LAN)
  • router1: B>* 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2, eth0 (forward path to pc2’s LAN)
- Hosts have correct defaults: pc1 via 195.11.14.1 and pc2 via 200.1.1.1 (get_host_net_config).
- Data path performs well: iperf from pc1 to pc2 sustains ~135–143 Mbit/s with no loss on the receiver.

Mechanism/Localization: The FRR BGP process on router1 and router2 is correctly advertising and installing each LAN prefix; traffic from pc2 to pc1 follows router2 → router1 → pc1 as expected, and vice versa.

Root cause: No routing fault present; the network currently forwards in both directions as designed.

Corrective fix: No changes required. If the one-way symptom reappears, capture simultaneous pings in both directions and check application/host firewalls on pc2, but routing/return path is confirmed correct at this time.
